### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1f4ebbc1aaddc2bc475357478bce84d3eea9bc55` — the merge of head `fd531c373a52c68892e75ff7a567022ac0fdd8d7` into base `d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1f4ebbc1aaddc2bc475357478bce84d3eea9bc55 && git checkout 1f4ebbc1aaddc2bc475357478bce84d3eea9bc55
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2 fd531c373a52c68892e75ff7a567022ac0fdd8d7 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2 && git merge --no-ff fd531c373a52c68892e75ff7a567022ac0fdd8d7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4b14a85048f45e52622eb520a00aaea2fe5bda2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `68ef9c717f74b5ae68f18f3a398713e346c6164c`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. The diff is three paths (`.changeset/env-action-bare-route-unheld-object.md`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`): no published schema, no governed path. The PR body and the changeset each carry the line-initial `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the review is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` line alone. Inputs read: card #32751 (body and all five comments, including the p1 re-grade and both claims), PR #32987 (body, file list, net diff at the head), and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read to judge the change, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The widening matches the card, and goes no wider.** Card Do-1 asks that the bare route resolve the environment's own item when no holder binds the object, without reading it through any holder's exact address. In the tree, `routeOwnerOfRefusedRead` changes one answer only: the `rung.length === 0` arm, when every candidate's own address answered and none owns the route. That arm used to answer `{ action: undefined, obj }` and now calls `readEnvironment()`. Every other arm is byte-identical: fewer than two candidates, a non-package candidate, a refused candidate address other than `not-held-by-qualifier`, an unread candidate, two owners on one rung, and a thrown read. `environmentOwnerOfUnheldRoute` never calls `readAt`, so it never touches a holder's address. It returns no `packageId`, so the dispatch is unqualified. Red line 2 holds.

**It cannot serve another package's action.** The function answers none whenever any packaged item of the name owns the route: `_packageId` set, and bound to the routed object or object-less. It serves only an item with no package. `ownsRoute` uses `standaloneActionOwnerKey`, the same ladder the outer `ownsRoute` reaches through the alias `standaloneActionObjectName`.

**It cannot serve a disabled package's action, and it honours ruling 6824698376 A.** The registry is read with `listItems('action', undefined, { includeDisabledPackages: true })`. `SchemaRegistry.listItems` filters disabled packages only when that flag is unset, so a disabled package's item bound to `lead` (or object-less) still blocks the environment item. That case is pinned in both registration orders.

**It cannot serve the platform's item or an item from another source.** The served item must also match an active `sys_metadata` row with no package, keyed `OWNER:NAME` through `environmentStoredActionNames`, the origin test the bare holder rule already uses. A package-less item with no row (host or plugin code) answers none, and that case is pinned. An engine with no store answers none: no `find`, or `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` naming `sys_metadata` through `listingNotServed`. Case 2's existing pin now also asserts no `degraded`. Any other store failure answers `degraded` (503, ADR-0110 D3), and that case is pinned.

**It does not bypass the 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT.** `bareRouteHolderRefusal` (two holders on this route's key) runs first and is unchanged. The new arm is reached only when no package candidate owns the route. Inside it, a packaged owner forces none rather than a pick, and among package-less owners the function serves exactly one per rung (bound before object-less) or none. It never chooses between two holders. `admitResolvedAction` still answers any `refusal` with 409 before it reads the declaration.

**The permission and record-access checks still run on the new path.** The new answer has the same shape as every other declared answer, `{ action, obj }`, and goes into `admitResolvedAction` like any other. That function does not branch on how a declaration was resolved, so every gate runs in its usual order: ADR-0106 visibility, the AI-door rules, the ADR-0066 D4 capability gate against the environment item's own `requiredPermissions`, the ADR-0126 activation consult, `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` (a handler that another declared action owns is refused), the type check, the ADR-0104 param contract, and the subject-record load under the caller's RLS. `refuseDispatchToDisabledObject` still runs before resolution.

**The tests pin the served case and its neighbours.** The new `[#32751]` describe sits beside case 2, as card Do-2 asks. It pins:
- the newly served case: `lead` serves the environment item with no package and its handler runs, in both orders;
- the CONTROL: `account` answers A's item and `contact` answers B's, in both orders;
- an object-less environment item, in both orders;
- a disabled holder on `lead`, which stays none;
- the platform item with no row, which stays none;
- a failing store read, which answers `degraded`.

The PR body reports an ablation per guard, each with a failing pin. That is consistent with the pins in the diff, but this review did not re-run it.

- **should-fix — the claim that the action runs is proven only with a hand-bound handler and a hand-registered item.** The served pin calls `engine.registerAction('lead', 'approve', …)` itself, and `shipPackageless` registers the registry item directly. On a booted kernel, `ObjectQLPlugin.resyncAuthoredActionsNow` filters out every authored action for which `isArtifactShippedAction` is true. That predicate asks `registry.getArtifactItem('action', name)` by NAME alone, so any installed package that ships `approve` (here A and B) stops the environment's `lead:approve` row from being bound. `executeRegisteredAction` has no fallback to the body. A script-bodied environment action on such a route would therefore get past every gate and then return 404 at dispatch ("Action 'approve' on object 'lead' not found"), where today it answers no declaration. That outcome is fail-closed but is not "可执行" as the card's 验证 line asks. Flow, declarative-update and same-origin `api` actions do not depend on that binding. The code is in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, outside this diff and its claimed surface. Before merge: either measure the full path on a booted kernel (stored row, then boot hydration through `registerOverlay`, then resync, then the route), or file the binding gap as its own card and narrow the PR's FROM → TO wording from "its handler runs" to "its declaration is served".
- **nit — the new code reads the registry copy, not a protocol read.** A comment in the same function (#25308) says the registry copy is not consulted when the protocol has a by-name read. The jsdoc explains why the protocol cannot answer here, and the disabled-package half of that rule is covered by `includeDisabledPackages`. Even so, the served body is the registry's, so no protocol-side serving rule applies to it. Today the risk is contained: `registerOverlay` does not register a declined package-less row of a sealed name, and the store check requires an active package-less row. The way out is the dev's out-of-scope finding (a): the `_env` address answers 404 here. Once that is fixed, this path can ask `_env` instead of the registry.
- **nit — two neighbours are not pinned with the environment item present.** One is an enabled third package bound to `lead`, which keeps its existing answer. The other is a candidate address answering `not-held-by-qualifier`, where the bare refusal stands. In both cases the code never reaches the new arm, but a pin would show that the new arm does not pre-empt either answer.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` `patch`. AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3) says a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. The level matches the declarations.

Confirmed: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, with the arm from the closed pair. It is not `no (narrowing)`, so the face stays declaration at `TIER_DEFAULT` and no ④ is owed. The changeset text matches the tree: FROM no declaration TO the environment's own action with no package, in either order, never at a holder's address; holders' routes unchanged; a package binding the route (a disabled one included) stays no declaration; an item with no row stays no declaration; a failing store read answers 503.

- **nit — the changeset leaves out one served shape.** Row 3 of the PR's FROM → TO table (the environment's object-less item answers `lead`) is a widened answer the changeset never names; it speaks only of an action "on a third object (`lead`)". Add one sentence so the CHANGELOG lists the widening completely.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Scope: the three paths sit inside the claimed file surface (`action-execution.ts`, the addressing test, `.changeset/**`). Nothing changes in `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/objectql` or `packages/spec`, and no governed path is touched.
- Red line 2 (never served as, or read through, a holder's exact address) holds. Ruling 6824698376 A (a disabled package is still a holder) holds. Seat ruling B's residual (the execution face beside a package-less item) is left as it was, and the PR body says so.
- CI on the head is not green:
  - `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` fails with `check:closing-target-claim`: the card had no `Claim:` naming `claude/project-thread-svxbge`. The restated claim (comment 6841742781) naming that branch was posted after the guard ran. A re-run should clear it, but none has run yet.
  - `Test Core (1/8)`, `(2/8)`, `(3/8)`, `(5/8)`, `(6/8)` and `(7/8)` are still in progress.
  - The PR is a draft. Merge waits for a green head.
- Out-of-scope findings from the dev, carried here so they are not lost: (a) `/actions/_env/lead/approve` answers 404 beside package holders; (b) with A disabled and B enabled beside the environment item, `/actions/contact/approve` answers no declaration on `main`. Neither changes with this PR, and neither has a card yet. The handler-binding gap in ① should be filed beside them.
- First-party count 0, as the PR states.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-svxbge`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH`

**VERDICT: PASS**

The answer kept is main's own: with only the environment's item and a disabled package on `lead`, main answers no declaration (measured). The body's ground is fixed in this PR (M1). The docblock and the pin's title are code and go to the follow-up card, so the head does not move under the contract review.
